body:
On a library whose metadata.db defines a custom column of datatype `rating` (e.g. label `myrating`,
name "My Rating"), the SPA renders TWO `role="slider"` controls that both carry `aria-label="Rating"`.
The group labels differ ("Rating" vs "My Rating") but the controls' own accessible names are identical.

Two consequences.

1. **Accessibility, which is the real one.** A screen-reader user hears "Rating" twice on the same page
   with nothing distinguishing them, and cannot tell the built-in rating from the custom column. The
   accessible name should incorporate the column's own name.

2. **It breaks three e2e specs on any such library** — `edit-rating.spec.ts:55` and `sp1-ux.spec.ts:3`
   (desktop) fail with `strict mode violation: locator('[role="slider"][aria-label="Rating"]') resolved
   to 2 elements`. The specs are not wrong; the DOM is ambiguous.

OBSERVED 2026-08-28 against an image built from feat/1939-my-library, running the repo's own
`local-dev` seed library, which defines `6|myrating|My Rating|rating`. NOT caused by that branch: its
diff touches no rating source file (`git diff origin/main...HEAD -- frontend/src | grep -i rating`
returns nothing), and CI is green on these specs because the CI seed has no rating custom column.

That divergence is itself worth noting: the local seed exercises a configuration CI never sees, so this
class of defect can only be caught locally today.
title: A rating-type custom column renders a second control with the identical accessible name 'Rating'
